feature.label: General SEM PLS Higher-Order Construct Point Estimates

claim.supported_scope: One non-nested second-order HOC in a raw, listwise, standardized, path-weighted, single-group recursive General SEM PLS model, using the exact repeated, extended-repeated, embedded two-stage, or disjoint two-stage approach and HCM-type matrix documented by this method.
claim.estimand: Approach-specific HOC component loadings or weights, formative component-score collinearity, authored structural paths touching the HOC, and extended-repeated direct, technical-indirect, and total effects.
assumptions: Every lower-order component is an ordinary Mode A or Mode B composite matching the first term of the HCM type.
The structural model is recursive and contains exactly one HOC with at least two unique lower-order components.
Generated aliases, component scores, and technical paths are execution artifacts and remain distinct from researcher-authored hypotheses.
exclusions: Nested or multiple HOCs, hybrid execution, HOC interactions, feedback, groups, case weights, matrix input, PLSc, and permutation are excluded.
Disjoint two-stage lower-order components must remain measurement-only in the final substantive graph.
This point cell makes no resampling-inference or causal claim.
warnings: Approach and HCM type determine whether component relationships are interpreted as loadings or weights.
SmartPLS documentation is used for comparable terminology and workflow scope, not as a numerical oracle.

equations.expression: eta_H = sum_j w_j eta_j for formative HOC relationships; eta_j = lambda_j eta_H + epsilon_j for reflective HOC relationships

references.citation: Becker, Klein, and Wetzels (2012), Hierarchical Latent Variable Models in PLS-SEM
Independent validation-only higher-order PLS reference fixtures

simulations.design: Frozen reflective and formative component fixtures covering the allowed approach/type matrix and mapped HOC paths.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen scenario-indexed inputs; the production and independent implementations receive the same rows and declarations.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Mapped supported estimates agree within the frozen 1e-6 tolerance and unsupported shapes fail before publication.

boundaries.case: The approach, HCM type, or endogenous position is outside the documented matrix.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Preflight preserves the model and returns a corrective blocked decision.

boundaries.case: A component score is constant, nonfinite, singular, or cannot converge.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Execution publishes no completed result and identifies the failed stage.

boundaries.case: Rows, indicators, components, and relations are consistently reordered.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped scientific estimates and stable identities remain equivalent within tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same resident model, recipe, data, and cell are executed again.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The scientific result is identical apart from operational identifiers and timestamps.

boundaries.case: A stage, mapping, generated identity, estimate, method, capability, or digest is altered.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict schema-6 reopen rejects the result.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose exact HOC point cell differs from its resident plan.
Reject an unsupported HOC compiler, stage, or runner version.
Reject a result attached to different resident data.
Reject a changed archive member or analytical digest.
Reject unknown, duplicate, nonfinite, unordered, or incomplete HOC rows.
Preserve historical HOC identities without relabeling them as this cell.

persistence.legacy_policy: Existing legacy HOC projects and results retain their original identities; this cell applies only to an exact compiled General SEM v1 authority.

native.gui_cli_parity_rule: Every surface reads the same canonical result for the same resident model, recipe, data, plan, and exact capability cell.
accessibility_rules: Approach, HCM type, stage role, and loading-versus-weight meaning are available as text.
Generated technical paths are distinguished from authored hypotheses without relying on color or canvas position.
